name: io.github.inite-ai/inite-brain-service
title: INITE Brain
description: Long-term memory for AI agents: a bitemporal knowledge graph with cited answers.

tools.name: about_brain
tools.description: What this server is and what it can do, before you connect, and whether the server's own models (embeddings, chat) are currently available. Reads nothing and stores nothing.

tools.name: how_to_connect
tools.description: The two ways to authenticate, and what each is for. Reads nothing and stores nothing.

client.description: Which client you are configuring, if you want the specific instructions.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Semantic search over the company knowledge graph: the facts the query is about, the links between their entities and what was left out. Apply asOf for historical "what was true on X" queries. Embedding model on this tenant: set per workspace.

asOf.description: Valid-time as-of: facts true at this ISO 8601 moment (a retraction dated before it hides the fact; a fact learned after it still shows — not a knowledge snapshot)

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

detail.description: focus (default): only what the query is about, as facts or the source turn, whichever is shorter. compact: every fact of the matched entities, with entity ids. full: adds ids, scores, trust keys

tools.name: search_multi_hop
tools.description: Planner-LLM decomposes the query into ≤ maxHops anchored sub-queries; later hops are anchored to the running entity set. Built for questions that combine evidence across turns / sessions, or that require reasoning over multiple entities ("tenants who complained in April AND upgraded after"). Set synthesize=true to get a grounded answer with citations alongside the per-hop trace. Returns the hops, the answer when asked, and the evidence as focus lines. Embedding model on this tenant: set per workspace.

maxHops.description: Hard cap on planner hops (default 3, capped at 5 — beyond that latency dominates)

synthesize.description: Run the synthesizer over the final entity set and return a grounded answer with citations

synthesisGuardrails.description: Override guardrails when synthesize=true: strict closes to null on partial; lenient returns the answer with the verifier verdict; off skips the verifier

asOf.description: Valid-time as-of: facts true at this ISO 8601 moment (a retraction dated before it hides the fact; a fact learned after it still shows — not a knowledge snapshot)

detail.description: answer (default): the answer and its citations, or the evidence when there is none. full: adds every hit with scores and ids

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: tenant-global plus this user's personal facts; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: graph_retrieve
tools.description: Resolves the named entities by canonical name, walks their 1-hop neighbourhood over knowledge_edge, and returns facts across seeds ∪ neighbours, optionally filtered by predicate hints. Works from entities named up front and returns what the graph holds around them ("who runs engineering at Acme" — the answer lives on a neighbour, not on Acme itself). Seeds score 1.0, neighbours 0.7; soft-fails to an empty result.

entityNames.description: Canonical names of the entities to anchor on

query.description: Free-text fallback used to resolve seeds when a name does not match exactly

predicateHints.description: Prefer facts with these predicates (non-matching neighbour facts are dropped, seed facts kept at lower score)

asOf.description: Valid-time as-of: facts true at this ISO 8601 moment (a retraction dated before it hides the fact; a fact learned after it still shows — not a knowledge snapshot)

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: synthesize
tools.description: Runs hybrid search then feeds the retrieved facts to a generator LLM that produces a citation-bearing answer (each claim ends with [factId]); a verifier LLM then judges whether every claim is supported. Three guardrail modes: strict (default) returns null on partial / unsupported / verifier outage (fail-closed); lenient returns the answer alongside the verifier verdict; off skips the verifier. Returns a direct natural-language answer rather than raw search results. Embedding model on this tenant: set per workspace.

limit.description: Top-K facts fed to the generator (default 10)

asOf.description: Valid-time as-of: facts true at this ISO 8601 moment (not a knowledge snapshot)

detail.description: answer (default): the answer and its citations, or the evidence when there is none. full: adds every hit with scores and ids

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: tenant-global plus this user's personal facts; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: memory_diff
tools.description: Returns everything brain learned, unlearned, or replaced between two ISO 8601 cursors [from, to). createdFacts = new active facts; retractedFacts = facts marked retracted in-window with no successor; changedFacts = facts that were superseded by another (carries before+after); newEntities = entities created in-window; forgottenEntities = GDPR-erased tombstones; lapsedExpectations = temporary states (ill, away) whose expected end passed in-window with nothing confirming or ending them — worth asking about. Driving use case: "what changed since the last conversation?" Scope with entityIds and/or predicates to narrow the diff to a feature surface. Window is half-open; consecutive diffs over adjacent windows never double-count.

entityIds.description: Scope to these entities (short or full ids)

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

detail.description: text (default): the changes per entity, one line each. full: JSON with ids

tools.name: get_entity_profile
tools.description: One entity: canonical name, type and what brain holds about it now; detail "full" adds externalRefs, the ids of its records in the originating vertical.

entityId.description: Brain entity id (knowledge_entity:...) or short id

asOf.description: Valid-time as-of: facts true at this ISO 8601 moment (not a knowledge snapshot)

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

detail.description: text (default): with userId, current state as beliefs, disputes and an attribute index. compact: every current fact. full: JSON with ids

tools.name: get_entity_timeline
tools.description: Chronological audit of all facts brain has learned about this entity, including retracted ones. Useful for "what did we know when" investigations.

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

detail.description: text (default): the scenes its facts came from and the state changes in each, then the rest. compact: JSON events with ids. full: adds sources

tools.name: summarize_entity
tools.description: Returns a short one-line briefing about the entity — name, type, the most-confident active facts, external refs — suitable for dropping into an LLM context window. Caches in-process (per companyId / entityId / asOf / styleHint) so a hot entity touched across many turns doesn't reload the profile. styleHint='neutral' | 'sales' | 'support' are template-rendered (no LLM call). styleHint='client_llm' opts into MCP SAMPLING: brain asks the connected client (Claude Desktop / agent runtime) to write the one-liner with its own model — zero brain-side OpenAI cost, perfect for self-hosters who don't want brain holding an LLM key. Falls back to neutral template + sampledBy='local_template' when the client doesn't advertise sampling capability. A briefing in place of the full profile, timeline and competing facts.

entityId.description: Brain entity id (knowledge_entity:...) or short id

asOf.description: Summarize what was known at this ISO 8601 moment

styleHint.description: Phrasing register — 'neutral' (default), 'sales', 'support', or 'client_llm' (delegate to client-side LLM via MCP sampling; falls back to neutral template if client doesn't support sampling)

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: get_competing_facts
tools.description: Returns facts in COMPETING status — those the conflict resolver couldn't auto-supersede because two same-predicate bitemporal facts overlap in valid-time and are too cosine-close within margin. Grouped by (entityId, predicate); 2-fact groups are pairs the resolver left for adjudication, 3+-fact groups are multi-way disagreements escalated for human review. Answers "is this entity already conflicted on this predicate?" and can drive an in-product reviewer queue. asOf filters to disagreements that were live at that moment.

entityId.description: Brain entity id (knowledge_entity:...) or short id

asOf.description: Show what was competing at this ISO 8601 moment

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: preflight a user-scoped record_fact against tenant-global priors PLUS this user's personal ones. Omit for tenant-global candidates (matches record_fact's userId)

tools.name: detect_contradiction
tools.description: Dry-run preflight against fn::resolve_fact. Answers "if I were to record this fact right now, what would the resolver decide?" without writing to the database. wouldOutcome ∈ {INSERTED, SUPERSEDED, COMPETING, REJECTED}; reasoning explains which rule fired (semantics class, score gap vs margin, cosine threshold, etc); opposingFacts lists the same-predicate priors the resolver would have weighed against. Useful where the cost of a contested write is high (e.g. agent loops that pay an ingest credit). Fidelity: this preflight uses the SEED source-trust table and authority 0 — the live resolver scores opponents with the learned domain-scoped rates (migration 0045) and declared source authority (migration 0046), so predictions can differ for sources with conflict history or a registered authLevel.

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: preflight a user-scoped record_fact against tenant-global priors PLUS this user's personal ones. Omit for tenant-global candidates (matches record_fact's userId)

tools.name: get_fact
tools.description: Read a single fact as stored — predicate (aspect), object (statement), confidence, validity window, source attribution (vertical / recorder / conversationId), and lifecycle state. Retracted facts still resolve (retracted: true) — "why did I stop remembering this" is part of the trust story; only visibility fences turn into not-found. groundingStatus (grounded | ungrounded) appears on facts stamped by the claim-grounding plane (EVIDENCE_GROUNDING_STAMP); legacy rows carry no key. Same shape as GET /v1/facts/:id. Takes a factId as returned by searches and writes and returns the full trust record behind it.

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: get_fact_provenance
tools.description: Return the grounding provenance behind one fact: the verbatim conversation turns it was derived from (episodes, chronological, with char-span quotes when the deriver stamped them). When the server runs with the recursive-closure flag the response additionally carries derivedFacts + closure (the transitive derivedFrom support graph); a plain deployment returns episodes only — the response is a passthrough of GET /v1/facts/:id/provenance, no field filtering. Traversal depth is a server-side policy (flag + caps), not a caller knob. Lets a surprising fact be audited before it is trusted or retracted.

userId.description: Whose memory: this user's personal facts beside the tenant-global ones; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: find_related_entities
tools.description: Get entities connected to the given one via the knowledge graph.

asOf.description: Bitemporal edge cutoff — connections as they were believed at this ISO 8601 moment (mirrors GET /v1/entities/:id/connections?asOf=)

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: results include tenant-global relations plus this user's personal ones; omit for tenant-global only (fail-closed)

tools.name: match_procedure
tools.description: Cosine-matches procedural memory (curated 'how to' patterns the operator recorded) against a free-text context query. Returns top-K procedures sorted by similarity DESC then priority ASC. Surfaces the behaviour rules that apply to a context — e.g. "user asks about pricing" → "mention they're on platinum tier; they get 20% off". Procedural memory is the third tier alongside facts (semantic) and episodes (timeline).

tools.name: list_procedures
tools.description: Paginated listing of procedural memory for admin/review UIs. Sorted by priority ASC, createdAt DESC. Set includeRetired=true to see soft-deleted rows.

tools.name: search_communities
tools.description: Cosine-matches the query against topic-community summaries — the coarse retrieval scope. A community is a cluster of related entities (label propagation over the entity graph) with one rolled-up summary. Suited to broad questions ("what do we know about X domain"): it returns an overview of a domain rather than individual facts. Communities are (re)built off-hours by the dreams loop; an empty result means clustering has not run or the graph is too sparse.

tools.name: list_communities
tools.description: Paginated listing of topic communities, largest first. Each row carries a label, a rolled-up summary, and the member count. Gives the knowledge map at a glance.

tools.name: find_entity_communities
tools.description: Returns the topic communities a given entity is a member of. Places an entity in its broader context — which clusters / themes it participates in — and leads from one entity to the wider neighbourhood the cluster summarises.

tools.name: why
tools.description: Return the design decisions, rationale, invariants and gotchas recorded against a code anchor — the non-derivable engineering "why" a parser cannot recover from source. The anchor is a SCIP-style symbol string ("pkg/namespace/symbol") or a file path ("repo/path/file.ts"). Pass asOf to recall what was known at a past instant (bitemporal). Returns found:0 with empty memory when nothing is recorded.

symbol.description: Code anchor — SCIP-style symbol or file path

asOf.description: Bitemporal cursor — recall what was known as of this instant

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: tenant-global decisions plus this user's own; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: recall_decisions
tools.description: Find recorded design decisions / rationale / invariants / gotchas by NL topic ("why do we resolve facts through one gateway?"), across ALL code anchors — a semantic search over code-memory, rather than one known anchor. Returns matches with their code anchor + kind, ranked by relevance.

query.description: Natural-language topic to recall the "why" for

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: tenant-global decisions plus this user's own; omit for tenant-global only

tools.name: get_source_reputation
tools.description: Return everything brain knows ABOUT a source (not its facts): the operator-declared identity (type, authLevel — authority in conflict resolution), the learned per-domain agreement rates (domain = predicate; null domain = the global blended rate; rates need >=8 samples before the resolver trusts them over the neutral 0.5), and the reputation-over-time history. sourceKey is `vertical:recorder` (recorder falls back to `_`) — the same key facts carry in trustSnapshot.sourceKey. Shows how much weight a fact whose trustSnapshot looks surprising deserves.

tools.name: workspace_status
tools.description: The tenant this credential writes to (companyId, its display name, whether it is a personal workspace), what is already in its memory (entities, active facts, facts recorded in the last 7 days), how many Domain Packs are installed, for a user-bound connection who the user is in this memory (`user.name` — the name the memory has learned from them, null until it has), and `nextSteps` — the setup actions that would actually change something, derived from that state rather than a stored checklist (including asking the user how to address them, once, and recording it). Also `serverModels`: whether the server's own models (embeddings, chat) are available right now, with a notice when they are not. Answers "which workspace am I writing to?" and explains why memory answers may look emptier than expected.

tools.name: record_fact
tools.description: Records one fact about an entity directly; the memory settles it against the facts it holds (INSERTED / SUPERSEDED / COMPETING). Most facts arrive through ingestion.

expectedUntil.description: When a temporary state with no stated end (ill, away) should be over; not an end: the fact stays current

userId.description: Per-user scope: the fact (and a vertical+id entity) belongs to this user only

conversationId.description: Conversation the fact was observed in; marks it grounded

evidence.description: Up to 10 pointers to observations behind the claim; marks it grounded

ref.description: The pointer itself — id, URL, path, sha…

tools.name: link_entities
tools.description: Insert an edge between two entities. `kind` is the edge type — `identity_of` merges the `from` entity into `to` (cross-vertical identity reconciliation), other typed edges (`paid_for`, `mentioned_in`, `worked_with`, …) are surfaced in related-entity reads and contribute to PPR / SubgraphRAG context. Most edges come from event ingestion; this inserts one directly. identity_of rejects a request that names the same end twice and any merge that would close a cycle; declaring an identity that already holds answers `alreadyIdentical: true` with no edge, so a replay is safe.

tools.name: retract_fact
tools.description: Mark a fact as no longer believed. Cascades to facts derived from this one. Does not delete; the row remains for audit.

retractedBy.description: Who initiated the retraction — mirrors the REST RetractFactDto. Omit for the pre-existing default ({source: 'system'}); pass {source: 'human', userId} when relaying an operator/user decision so the audit trail records the real initiator

tools.name: record_procedure
tools.description: Record a 'how to' pattern that is surfaced when a similar context appears later. trigger = the context phrase the rule should match against (e.g. "user asks about pricing"); action = the behaviour to apply (e.g. "mention they're on platinum tier; they get 20% off"). priority orders ties when multiple procedures match the same context (lower is higher priority; default 100). decayHalfLifeDays is a forward hook for v0.2 relevance decay; v1 ignores it at read time.

sourceKind.description: Audit tag for who recorded this — default operator

tools.name: retire_procedure
tools.description: Mark a procedural memory row as retired (sets retiredAt). A retired procedure is no longer matched or listed by default. For a rule that no longer applies — distinct from a hard delete because the row stays for audit.

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Capture the non-derivable engineering "why" about a code location: a design decision, its rationale, an invariant that must hold, or a gotcha. Anchored to a SCIP-style symbol or file path (NOT line numbers — survives edits). Stored as a bitemporal typed fact: re-recording a `decided` / `invariant` for the same anchor SUPERSEDES the prior one (decision evolution over time), while `because` / `gotcha` accumulate. Attach commit / location for provenance.

symbol.description: Code anchor — SCIP-style symbol or file path

kind.description: decided = a design decision (supersedes prior); because = rationale; invariant = a constraint that must hold (supersedes prior); gotcha = a non-obvious trap (accumulates)

text.description: The decision / rationale / invariant / gotcha text

commit.description: Commit SHA this was decided in (provenance)

validFrom.description: When the decision took effect — defaults to now

tools.name: take_memory_work
tools.description: Returns the next batch of work the memory left for a connected model, in this order: predicate_semantics (new attributes: one value at a time or several), media_reading (images to read: their text verbatim and what they show; the images follow as image blocks), extraction (stored documents to read into facts), fact_resolution (new facts beside the memory facts they resemble: same, replaces, contradicts or unrelated), entity_match (pairs of entities that may be one thing), fact_conflict (pairs of competing facts), fact_corroboration (pairs of facts that may state one thing twice), scene_summary (conversation scenes to summarise), safety_reading (a person’s own words read for a risk of suicide or self-harm), affect_reading (how a consenting person seemed to feel, from their own words), belief_statement (remembered states to phrase as a sentence). A batch holds the systemPrompt and userContent the server model would have been sent, the JSON schema of the reply, how many items it covers, and the signed work token its reply is submitted with, valid until expiresAt. Returns {work: null} when nothing is waiting.

userId.description: Per-user memory scope: only this user's memory. Omit for tenant-global

kinds.description: Only these kinds; all by default

tools.name: submit_memory_work
tools.description: Stores a model's JSON reply to a batch of memory work, with its work token. The server applies it with its own code: extraction replies are grounded against the text it handed out, resolved and committed; attribute classifications update the vocabulary; verdicts link identical entities or supersede the losing fact; scene summaries and belief sentences are validated and written; an image's reading is stored with the image and read into facts. An item whose evidence changed since it was handed out is skipped and counted stale, so a batch applied twice changes nothing the second time. Returns counts for the batch. A bad, expired or foreign token is refused.

result.description: The reply object, matching the schema
